articles.title: Imposto do Pecado: Governo define alíquotas para bebidas e cigarros | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta prevê a manutenção da atual carga tributária sobre os produtos que causam danos à saúde no próximo ano, período de transição. Lista inclui bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros.
articles.summary: A MP do Imposto do Pecado define alíquotas para bebidas e cigarros, mantendo a carga atual até 2027 para compensar gastos bilionários com saúde e meio ambiente.
articles.body:
O governo federal publicou nesta quarta-feira (4) a medida provisória (MP) do Imposto Seletivo, também conhecido como "imposto do pecado". A medida foi publicada em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União na noite desta quarta.

A proposta prevê a manutenção da atual carga tributária sobre os produtos que causam danos à saúde no próximo ano , período de transição. Posteriormente, a partir de 2028, a ideia é que a taxação aumente.

🔎 Criado pela reforma tributária sobre o consumo, o imposto do pecado começará a ser cobrado em 2027 e tem o objetivo de encarecer produtos ou atividades que causam danos à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.

A lista inclui bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros. O novo imposto também incidirá sobre alguns veículos, conforme o nível de poluição, sobre a extração de bens minerais e sobre loterias, apostas e jogos de fantasy sports ( veja mais abaixo ).

🔎🔎 Medidas provisórias têm força de lei, mas precisam ser aprovadas pela Câmara dos Deputados e pelo Senado para se tornarem leis definitivas. O prazo inicial é de 60 dias, prorrogável por mais 60. A contagem é suspensa durante o recesso do Congresso.

O governo federal afirmou que o regime estabelecido pela medida provisória terá caráter temporário e ficará em vigor até 31 de dezembro de 2027.

Nesse período, as alíquotas do Imposto Seletivo de veículos, aeronaves, embarcações, produtos fumígenos, bebidas alcoólicas e bebidas açucaradas corresponderão às atuais alíquotas do Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI), após a aplicação de fatores específicos de conversão.

"A adequação considera as diferenças entre as bases de incidência dos dois tributos, de modo a preservar o nível efetivo da tributação durante a transição".

Até 31 de maio de 2027, o governo deve encaminhar ao Congresso um projeto de lei com a definição das alíquotas para serem aplicadas a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2028.

Como o Imposto eletivo tem noventena, ou seja, demora 90 dias para entrar em vigor depois de ser aprovado pelo Legislativo , o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, informou nesta terça-feira (3) que também combinou com os setores que, nesse meio tempo, o IPI continuará sendo cobrado sobre esses produtos — como forma de evitar perda de arrecadação.

A medida consta em uma Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) enviada ao Congresso nesta quarta.

Segundo a Casa Civil, a medida foi feita "a fim de evitar a desoneração sobre produtos gravosos à saúde, a exemplo de cigarros".

bebidas alcóolicas álcool garrafas bar drinks — Foto: Pexels

Para 2027, a equipe econômica estima arrecadar R$ 41,9 bilhões com esse tributo, segundo a proposta de Orçamento enviada ao Congresso .

Com a cobrança do Imposto Seletivo e da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), outro tributo criado pela reforma e que começará a ser cobrado em 2027, o governo busca manter a arrecadação estável em relação ao Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

Veja alguns dos principais produtos afetados

A medida provisória prevê uma alíquota diferente para cada produto. A intenção é que a mudança não altere o valor total pago atualmente em tributos.

🍺O governo define um imposto seletivo de 4,2% para a cerveja. Para o vinho, propõe uma taxa de 8%. Para os cigarros, a alíquota é de 66,7%, mais R$ 3,50 por maço.

Para bebidas açucaradas, como refrigerantes, por exemplo, a alíquota é de 2,6%.

➡️Levantamento da Fiocruz, citado pelo Ministério da Saúde, diz que, em 2019, o consumo de álcool custou R$ 18,8 bilhões, dos quais R$ 1,1 bilhão relativo a custos federais diretos com hospitalizações e procedimentos ambulatoriais no SUS, e R$ 17,7 bilhões à perda de produtividade pela mortalidade prematura, licenças e aposentadorias precoces decorrentes de doenças associadas ao consumo de álcool, perda de dias de trabalho por internação hospitalar e licença médica previdenciária.

➡️No Brasil, segundo o Ministério da Saúde, as doenças relacionadas ao tabagismo geram um custo indireto de R$ 86,3 bilhões por ano, o que resulta em um gasto total anual de R$ 153,5 bilhões para o governo, o equivalente a 1,6% do PIB. "Em contrapartida, a arrecadação de tributos federais na venda de cigarros é de apenas R$ 8 bilhões por ano, o que evidencia desequilíbrio entre os gastos com a saúde e a arrecadação gerada pela comercialização do produto", diz.

➡️Considerando as bebidas ultraprocessadas, como refrigerantes, isotônicos e refrescos, o governo estimou, em estudo para embasar o uso do imposto seletivo, que os custos contabilizados para o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) com o tratamento de doenças associadas ao consumo desses produtos são estimados em quase R$ 3 bilhões ao ano.

➡️Produtores nacionais dizem que as bebidas alcoólicas, por exemplo, já têm taxação alta no Brasil, com carga tributária variando de 40% a mais de 80% do preço do produto, e avaliam que um eventual aumento dos impostos cobrados pressionará as margens de lucro, podendo gerar repasses aos preços, demissões e estímulo ao mercado ilegal.

articles.title: Paraguaios protestam após quebra de banco digital Ueno  | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo prepara medidas para ressarcir depositantes, enquanto investigação sobre a instituição amplia a pressão sobre o presidente Santiago Peña.
articles.summary: Maior emissor de cartões de crédito do país, Ueno enfrenta problemas financeiros e investigações. Crise também aumenta a pressão sobre o governo de Santiago Peña.
articles.body:
Milhares de paraguaios foram às ruas de Assunção nesta terça-feira (3) para exigir acesso ao próprio dinheiro após uma crise envolvendo o Ueno Bank, um dos maiores bancos digitais do país, com cerca de 3 milhões de clientes.

O Banco Central do Paraguai iniciou um procedimento para proteger os depositantes e limitar os impactos da crise sobre o sistema financeiro. O caso levou à renúncia do presidente do BC, Carlos Carvallo, e aumentou a pressão sobre o governo de Santiago Peña.

A instituição, maior emissora de cartões de crédito do Paraguai, enfrenta problemas financeiros e é alvo de investigações. Após ajustes em seus balanços, o índice de solvência do banco, que indica sua capacidade de cumprir obrigações financeiras, caiu para menos da metade do mínimo exigido por lei.

Manifestantes foram às ruas no Paraguai depois da crise no banco digital Ueno — Foto: Daniel Duarte / AFP

A crise afetou diretamente os clientes. Nesta terça-feira, quem procurou as agências do Ueno encontrou as portas fechadas. Aplicativos e cartões também deixaram de funcionar, prejudicando inclusive aposentados que recebem benefícios do governo por meio da instituição.

O banco administra aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em recursos públicos no Paraguai, incluindo valores do Instituto de Previdência Social (IPS) e de outros fundos de previdência pública.

Diante da situação, clientes foram às ruas para cobrar a liberação do dinheiro depositado no banco. Houve confrontos entre manifestantes e policiais em Assunção.

"Estamos exigindo acesso ao dinheiro que temos aqui no banco Ueno", disse à agência Reuters Manuel Cáceres, morador de Ñemby, nos arredores da capital paraguaia. "Infelizmente, muita gente, inclusive eu, está passando a manhã assim."

Para tentar conter os efeitos da crise, o presidente Santiago Peña anunciou um acordo com líderes do Congresso para acelerar a votação de um projeto que permitirá utilizar recursos do Fundo de Garantia do país para ressarcir os depositantes.

Peña também afirmou que a medida deve assegurar a devolução de recursos públicos mantidos no banco, incluindo valores do IPS e de outros fundos de previdência.

Manifestantes foram às ruas no Paraguai depois da crise no banco digital Ueno. — Foto: DANIEL DUARTE/AFP

O Ministério Público solicitou a abertura de uma investigação criminal sobre o caso e a prisão de oito pessoas ligadas ao Ueno. Os detidos incluem integrantes da direção e do grupo controlador da instituição.

O banco já vinha sendo alvo de uma fiscalização mais rigorosa nos últimos meses. Órgãos reguladores investigavam se o Ueno havia financiado indiretamente a venda de uma carteira de ativos de uma empresa ligada ao Grupo Vázquez, seu controlador. A instituição negou participação na operação.

O episódio também aumentou a pressão sobre o governo de Peña. O presidente paraguaio foi sócio do grupo controlador do Ueno até março de 2025.

Além disso, Carvallo, que comandou o Ueno até agosto de 2023, vinha sendo criticado por parlamentares por sua atuação na supervisão da instituição. As críticas também atingiam o Banco Central, cuja cúpula foi alvo de pedidos de afastamento por congressistas, após rejeitar um relatório sobre o Ueno por considerá-lo incompleto.

Ao anunciar sua renúncia, Carvallo afirmou que permaneceria no cargo durante o procedimento adotado pelas autoridades para lidar com a crise.

Segundo ele, sua saída ajudaria a reduzir as controvérsias em torno do Banco Central e permitiria que a instituição e a Superintendência de Bancos atuassem sem disputas políticas e pressão da imprensa.

O Banco Central afirmou que o caso do Ueno é isolado e não indica problemas mais amplos no sistema financeiro paraguaio. Peña também tentou afastar preocupações sobre a estabilidade do setor.

"Este é um caso específico de uma entidade, não do sistema financeiro nacional", declarou o presidente.

Peña acrescentou que os responsáveis pelo caso "devem responder perante o Judiciário, sem exceções e sem privilégios".

A Superintendência de Bancos deverá nomear auditores para avaliar a situação dos ativos do Ueno.

A crise também chegou ao mercado financeiro. As preocupações com o banco pressionaram os títulos em dólar emitidos pela instituição, com vencimento em 2031, além dos títulos da dívida pública paraguaia.

articles.title: Selling your home could cost you more than $80,000. Here's the breakdown.
articles.summary: Homeowners are spending more to sell their home, and many underestimate what it will cost to prep, market, and close a deal.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Homeowners are spending more to sell their home, and many underestimate what it will cost to prep, market, and close a deal. Factor in a growing number of buyer's markets, and sellers' profits are being squeezed too.

Owners who put their house on the market in the past three years shelled out an average of nearly $82,000 to sell their home, up 22% from 2025, according to new research by Clever Real Estate.

Here are the numbers sellers will want to consider before listing.

Homeowners expected to spend just under $27,000 to sell, but the actual costs were more than three times that amount, the Clever Real Estate research found.

"The biggest selling costs that most people typically underestimate are closing costs, such as title insurance, transfer taxes, and document prep," Jaime Seale of Clever Real Estate said. "The charges are often bundled into a single bill, so they don't know exactly how much they're being charged for each service. When added all together, the costs add up to a hefty bill most aren't expecting."

However, while closing costs averaged over $11,000, the biggest expense was home improvements to prepare the house for the market, topping $27,600.

According to the study, these are the average expenses recent sellers faced:

Repairs, improvements, or renovations: $27,649

Listing agent commission on the average-priced home: $13,875

Buyer's agent commission on the average-priced home: $13,573

Higher mortgage rates are giving buyers leverage in negotiations. As a result, the study found that a large proportion of sellers are looking to sell a home quickly (49%), rather than simply prioritizing maximum profit (48%).

"Offering concessions can speed up a sale and ease the up-front financial burden on buyers, while letting sellers hold firm on price," Seale said. "How much sellers spend on concessions depends on their home and their local market, but among those who offered them, the value averaged $9,914."

It's been two years since the National Association of Realtors settled an antitrust lawsuit that was intended to lower real estate commissions. Before the August 2024 settlement, sellers traditionally paid the buyer's agent commission in a sale. That's in addition to the seller's agent fee.

"In practice, not much has changed," Seale said. "A majority of sellers still pay the buyer's Realtor fees, especially in this market when sellers must compete for buyers and attracting them is a top priority. Sellers should expect to pay about 5.46% of the final sale price on commission, divided between the listing agent (2.76%) and the buyer's agent (2.70%)."

On the average-priced home, that costs sellers $27,448.

For sellers: higher costs, lower profits

Seale noted that for sellers, the prevailing real estate market is raising costs and lowering profits.

"Many sellers list their homes expecting pandemic-era offers, only to find that buyers can no longer afford those prices. Selling costs then cut into an already smaller sale price, often by more than sellers anticipated. We found that 39% say their profit was less than expected because of the total cost to sell."

articles.title: Trump Media stock plunges 12% after Democrats sweep Congress
articles.summary: The ticker has served as a bellwether of the president's power, reflecting his outsized influence over all things politics, and his ability to attract capita...
articles.body:
Voters on Tuesday delivered a stunning rebuke to the Trump agenda, but markets produced a referendum of their own — on the president's eponymous stock.

Trump Media & Technology Group ( DJT ) stock, the home of the president's Truth Social platform, plunged over 12% during morning trading Wednesday. The ticker has served as a bellwether of the president's power, reflecting his outsized influence over all things politics, and his ability to attract capital and attention.

But the election results have shifted the balance of power. Democratic victories in battleground states and formerly Trump-voting districts have shattered the GOP's trifecta hold on Washington. And they have called into question Trump's own standing and effectiveness as party leader, chief executive, and business mogul.

The sudden drop in Trump Media suggests an answer to at least one of those questions: What happens to the company once Trump is out of power? The simplest response from Wall Street is that it will be worth a lot less.

But Trump Media's decline didn't begin on Election Day. Shares of the company are down nearly 60% for the year, as traffic on its marquee social media platform has waned. And, as the election made clear, the once MAGA-dominated political environment has changed.

Trump Media's plunge also gets at broader issues concerning the president's business relationships and what his critics describe as unethical financial entanglements.

Earlier this year, for instance, the company announced it would launch a tool that would give Wall Street clients faster access to Trump's Truth Social posts, where he often announces new policies and generates market-moving headlines.

Entering the lame-duck phase of his presidency means Trump has less power to steer policy, in turn making access to his preferred platform less sought-after.

Wall Street is also reacting to what will be a sudden shift in review authority come early next year. The Democratic takeover gives the president's opponents new avenues to launch investigations and apply fresh oversight to his business dealings.

articles.title: Trump Media Falls to All-Time Low As Republicans Lose Congress
articles.summary: President Donald Trump’s social media company and meme coin both plunged after Democrats won a decisive victory in the midterm elections, dinging the multibi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump's social media company and meme coin both plunged after Democrats won a decisive victory in the midterm elections, dinging the multibillion-dollar fortune of a president whose slew of new business ventures became a defining feature of his second term.

Trump Media & Technology Group Corp., the parent company of social media platform Truth Social, touched an all-time low of $5.03 on Wednesday. $TRUMP, the virtual token that Trump introduced days before his second inauguration, slid more than 10% in the past 24 hours, according to data provider CoinMarketCap.

The simultaneous drop in both assets — which trade heavily on retail speculation — signals investors may be anxious about the implications of the election for the businesses with links to the president, which are now expected to receive fresh congressional oversight.

For months, Democrats have signaled their appetite to pursue investigations into the president and his family's business interests if they prevail in either chamber, leaving any company connected to the first family as a potential target.

"LAWYER UP," Robert Garcia, the California Democrat in line to chair the House Oversight Committee, posted on social media as the results rolled in on Tuesday night.

The businesses account for meaningful wealth for the first family. Trump's stake in the social media company, which he holds through a trust controlled by his eldest son Donald Trump Jr, is worth about $600 million; the meme coin business accounts for about $83 million, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Trump shunned decades of norms for American presidents, drawing rebuke from the left for profiting from cryptocurrency ventures and business interests that bear his name while in office.

When the New York Times asked the president earlier this year about conflicts of interest in his second term, he said, "I found out that nobody cared." The White House has maintained that there are no conflicts of interests involving the president's business ventures.

Yet polling ahead of the midterms showed that government corruption, broadly, was a significant concern for voters. A Fox News poll found 60% of voters were extremely worried about government corruption, while a Gallup survey showed Americans' perceptions of government corruption in the US hit their highest level in 20 years, with 89% of respondents calling it widespread.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk CEO says CVS breakup has no material impact on the weight-loss drug giant
articles.summary: A CVS breakup will be a big deal for healthcare players.
articles.body:
For now, Novo Nordisk ( NVO ) CEO Mike Doustdar says it's business as usual for its weight-loss drug behemoth as healthcare giant CVS Health ( CVS ) undergoes a complicated breakup.

"In some ways, I would say I don't see a material impact for us other than now we have to of course have two different negotiations and two different groups of people that we will speak to about our products and making sure that it finds it in their formulary, but being a popular product company makes it a lot easier than otherwise," Doustdar said on Sozzi Unleashed .

CVS Health announced plans late Wednesday to break up its $117 billion healthcare empire into two standalone, publicly traded businesses. The planned separation reverses years of vertical integration, unwinding the 2018 landmark acquisition of insurer Aetna.

Under the plan, the retail pharmacy network and storefront operations will spin off into an independent company named CVS Pharmacy.

The other operation will house the Aetna health insurance business, Caremark pharmacy benefit manager, and primary care assets. The breakup is slated to be completed in the first half of 2028.

Doustdar added, "When you're selling products like ours that are in need of many patients, then almost everyone would like to work with you."

Follow Brian Sozzi on X @BrianSozzi , Instagram , and LinkedIn . Tips on stories? Email him at brian.sozzi@yahoofinance.com.

articles.title: Waymo confirms it’s shaking up its Uber relationship in January 2028
articles.summary: The change will set up direct competition in those markets, as Uber has many other autonomous vehicle partners on its network.
articles.body:
Waymo will end its exclusivity with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.

The robotaxi company will offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. Uber confirmed to TechCrunch Wednesday that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree. Waymo did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Mawakana's comments come after reporting earlier this year by the Financial Times that Waymo was looking to get out of its deal with Uber, which was set to expire in May 2028 . Mawakana told Bloomberg that Waymo initially partnered with Uber because the ride-hail giant offered scale. But the experience for riders has been "a little bit of a crapshoot," she said, especially because riders never know for sure if they're going to hail a robotaxi or a human-driven car.

"It's important for us to have that relationship with the rider. We've gotten that feedback from the riders in those markets," Mawakana said.

Uber — which has many robotaxi and other autonomous vehicle partners — told Bloomberg that it was Waymo's idea not to add an option in the ride-hail giant's app to book a robotaxi directly.

This story has been updated with new information from Uber , and to correct that Mawakana's comments were about the exclusivity.

articles.title: 'The money has to come from somewhere': Florida voters approve sweeping property tax cut, while tax revolts in Wyoming and Oklahoma fall short
articles.summary: Property tax relief efforts won big in Florida but fell short in Oklahoma and Wyoming as voters confronted the trade-offs between lowering taxes and reducing...
articles.body:
Voters in seven states weighed in on property tax relief measures on Tuesday, part of an ongoing property tax revolt that has developed in recent years as home prices and assessed values soared while incomes have largely failed to keep up. The outcomes were mixed, with voters in Florida and North Carolina overwhelmingly approving amendments designed to cut or cap taxes, while Wyoming and Oklahoma voters rejected tax-limiting measures.

The split results reflect the complicated trade-offs between limiting unpopular and fast-rising taxes and funding public services.

"Property tax bills are rising far faster than inflation and even home valuations," said Nicole Fox, a policy analyst at the Tax Foundation. "People are noticing."

The most sweeping effort to lower taxes came in Florida, where 62% of voters approved a major property tax cut that will increase the amount of a home's value that can be exempted from non-school homestead property taxes, effectively eliminating those taxes entirely in some parts of the state.

"What happened last night was a really big deal," said Danielle Blake, chief of residential and advocacy at Miami Realtors, which supported the Florida initiative, known as Amendment 3. "That is the voters speaking loud and clear that they want relief."

In North Carolina, an amendment requiring the General Assembly to pass legislation limiting how much local governments can raise property tax revenues from year to year passed with over 60% of the vote. And Louisiana voters approved ballot initiatives designed to provide property tax relief to select groups, including seniors.

But in Oklahoma, voters rejected a ballot question that sought to limit the growth in property tax assessment limits. A Wyoming amendment that would have cut property taxes by 50% for most homes also failed after critics, including the state's governor, argued that the cuts would decimate local services.

Municipalities across the country rely heavily on property taxes, which account for 70% or more of local revenues. Those taxes frequently fund popular services like infrastructure, parks, and public safety. Cutting them can mean municipalities must find another way to cover the shortfall or reduce services.

"If you eliminate [property taxes], the money has to come from somewhere else, or the service gets eliminated," said Bill Healey, 2026 president of the International Association of Assessing Officers.

articles.title: Outback steps in to save dozens of steakhouses after franchise owner files for bankruptcy
articles.summary: The steakhouse chain has around 115 franchised restaurants across the US
articles.body:
Outback Steakhouse's largest U.S. franchisee has filed for bankruptcy , putting 61 western restaurants up for sale as the chain's parent company seeks to take them over.

Out West Restaurant Group, also known as Cerca Trova Restaurant Group, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Monday after years of declining sales and rising costs. Its financial troubles date back to 2018, when falling restaurant traffic began eating into revenue. The pandemic further deepened the losses, with revenue plunging 35 percent in 2020, according to court filings .

The franchisee has reached a $26.3 million agreement with Outback's parent company, Bloomin' Brands, to sell its restaurants and assets. The deal serves as a "stalking horse" bid, establishing a minimum starting price that other potential buyers can attempt to beat during the bankruptcy process.

Bloomin' Brands is providing up to $5.5 million to keep the restaurants open during bankruptcy with no immediate changes expected for customers or employees.

The steakhouse chain has around 115 franchised restaurants in the U.S., along with about 544 company-owned locations. If Bloomin' Brands completes the acquisition, it would take direct control of more than half of Outback's remaining U.S. franchised restaurants, according to Restaurant Dive .

Bloomin' said it was "working closely with Out West, its lenders, and other stakeholders throughout the Bankruptcy Court-supervised process as it focuses on maintaining stability in Out West's restaurant operations, supporting Team Members and continuing to serve guests," Restaurant Dive reports.

The company said that buying Out West's restaurants "gives [Bloomin'] direct operational insight, allows it to invest in the units through its development initiatives, and to mitigate disruption to guests and employees."

Out West's restaurants are primarily located in the Southwest with locations in Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico and Colorado. The company also has significant creditors in California, according to bankruptcy filings cited by Restaurant Dive .

News of the bankruptcy filing comes as Outback revamps its menu and kitchen practices to improve food quality and win back diners.

The changes include adding a New York strip to its regular menu for the first time and introducing a thick-cut ribeye called the "Down Under Delmonico." Outback is also updating its cut specifications, hand-trimming techniques and seasoning methods for existing favorites, including its center-cut sirloin, Rockhampton ribeye and Victoria's barrel-cut filet mignon, the company said.

Bloomin' Brands also owns Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar.

articles.title: Snap Declines After Daily User Growth Falls Short of Estimates
articles.summary: Snap Inc. fell after the company reported third-quarter ad revenue and user growth that missed estimates, with Chief Executive Officer Evan Spiegel acknowled...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Snap Inc. fell after the company reported third-quarter ad revenue and user growth that missed estimates, with Chief Executive Officer Evan Spiegel acknowledging that "advertising revenue growth remains below our ambitions."

The company had 495 million daily active users through the period ending in September, compared with 493 million the prior quarter. User numbers missed analysts' expectations of 499 million.

Third-quarter revenue and a current-quarter forecast were in line with analyst expectations.

Revenue increased 14% to $1.72 billion in the quarter ended Sept. 30, the company said Wednesday, aligned with the average of estimates compiled by Bloomberg. Snap, which owns the Snapchat messaging app, projected fourth-quarter sales for an average of $1.97 billion, slightly exceeding analysts' projections for $1.96 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Shares of the Santa Monica, California-based company dropped more than 11% in aftermarket trading. The stock had been down 27% so far this year heading into Wednesday's report.

Spiegel said he is working to build Snap's advertising business after making performance improvements for "more durable growth" in the future, according to his prepared remarks for investors. He is also betting big on the company's AI-powered glasses, called Specs, unveiled in June. The company has been taking orders for the $2,195 gadgets and said it plans to begin shipments later this year.

Snap faces a challenging regulatory and legal environment, with countries considering social media bans for teens and users filing lawsuits alleging the companies behind these platforms have knowingly hooked and harmed minors with their products. "While outcomes remain uncertain, they may result in significant changes to our products and business practices," the company said.

articles.title: Flutter CEO Dan Taylor: Here's how prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket are disrupting FanDuel
articles.summary: Flutter's new CEO has a big hill to climb right out of the gate.
articles.body:
New Flutter ( FLUT ) CEO Dan Taylor won't have a honeymoon period as the FanDuel operator looks to jump-start its online betting business while also thwarting deep-pocketed, free-spending prediction markets sites like Kalshi and Polymarket.

"Marketing spend across the category was up 60%-plus in September and 50%-plus October. And a lot of that is driven by the incremental investment we're seeing from the prediction operators," Taylor said on Yahoo Finance. "But for us, we need to be really disciplined. We measure and track the returns we get from our marketing spend very closely, and we see good returns. We will be investing more because we see more opportunities to do so and the market is competitive."

Taylor took over as Flutter CEO on Oct. 1 after spending many years running the platform's international business.

"Our customers across the country, we are starting to see them use the product in a very similar way [to prediction markets]," Taylor said. "So the behaviors we're seeing on our prediction product in the OSB states and the non-OSB states, they're kind of pretty similar in terms of the mix of parlay bets, the mix of inplay, the types of things they're betting on are kind of similar."

Taylor faces an uphill battle given the increasing competition for betting dollars.

Flutter delivered modest top-line growth in the third quarter, generating a total group revenue increase of 2% to $3.874 billion.

Sales were led by a 6% increase in US revenue to $1.455 billion, driven by solid sportsbook and iGaming handle. International revenue remained essentially flat at $2.419 billion due to adverse customer-friendly sports results and regulatory headwinds.

Adjusted operating profits fell 25% from the prior year.

Flutter warned on weak sports results to start the fourth quarter both in the US and internationally. The company was forced to mark down its full-year revenue and operating profit outlooks.

Flutter stock still rose 3% on the session before closing Wednesday's trading slightly down.

articles.title: AMC Theatres Sets All-Time Record for Quarterly Revenue, Thanks to ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ and ‘The Odyssey’
articles.summary: The blockbuster success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” fueled a record-breaking quarter for AMC Theatres. Total revenue for the three-month...
articles.body:
The blockbuster success of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "The Odyssey" fueled a record-breaking quarter for AMC Theatres. Total revenue for the three-month period ended Sept. 30 hit $1.71 billion, up 31.6% from $1.30 billion a year earlier.

That marked the biggest sales haul ever posted by the world's largest cinema chain, eclipsing the previous all-time high of $1.60 billion established in the second quarter of 2026, led by "Project Hail Mary and "Michael." Prior to this year's rebound, AMC's quarterly revenue high-water mark was pro-COVID, set in the second quarter of 2019, when "Avengers: Endgame" was released and shattered any and all box office expectations.

AMC also swung to a profit: The company reported net income of $109.3 million, compared with a $298.2 million net loss in the third quarter of 2025. It logged earnings per share of 12 cents for the most recent quarter, after reporting a loss of 58 cents in the prior-year quarter.

"In recent years, where other key players in our industry collapsed, at AMC we repeatedly instead have talked about recovery. Today, we can finally say that AMC has recovered," AMC CEO Adam Aron said in a statement. "To our studio partners, lenders, business partners, employees and our millions of passionate shareholders, thank you for standing with us as we traveled through a long, and at times brutal, road. Mere survival was never the goal. Our goal ultimately was to thrive, and that is exactly and precisely where our focus now lies. We are highly energized by the tremendous opportunities ahead."

Aron attributed the better-than-expected quarter to several factors, including the rising popularity of premium large formats, the A-List subscription service and a resurgent box office. This summer was the best since COVID, as "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" became the third-highest grossing movie in history with $2.5 billion and Nolan's 'The Odyssey" powered to an astounding $1.8 billion. Overall domestic theatrical revenue has already eclipsed $8 billion, a milestone the industry didn't cross last year until December. With potential juggernauts like "Avengers: Doomsday," "Dune: Part III" and "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" still to come on the schedule, this year will easily be the biggest at the box office in post-pandemic times.

articles.title: AstraZeneca made $10 billion offer for obesity drugmaker Rhythm, sources say
articles.summary: By Sabrina Valle, Milana Vinn and Amy-Jo Crowley Nov 4 (Reuters) - AstraZeneca made an offer of about $10 billion to acquire obesity drugmaker Rhythm Pharmac...
articles.body:
By Sabrina Valle, Milana Vinn and Amy-Jo Crowley

Nov 4 (Reuters) - AstraZeneca made an offer of about $10 billion to acquire obesity drugmaker Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, according to three people ‌familiar with the matter.

AstraZeneca offered as much as $134 a share in the non-binding proposal, ‌including payments for milestone achievements, the people said.

The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Wednesday that AstraZeneca had made a $124-per-share ​offer for the company last month.

Shares of Rhythm closed up 28% at $110.68 on the news, giving it a market capitalization of about $7.64 billion.

The acquisition would be pursued through AstraZeneca's rare-disease business Alexion, which the company acquired for $39 billion in 2021 to expand beyond its core oncology and biopharmaceutical franchises, two ‌of the people said.

An AstraZeneca spokesperson ⁠declined to comment.

Representatives for Rhythm did not respond to a request for comment.

AstraZeneca CEO Pascal Soriot is seeking to shift investors' focus back to growth ⁠after a turbulent few months. The company, which has a $292 billion market value, faced some clinical trial setbacks, and reports of a potentially transformative deal with US rival Bristol Myers Squibb had weighed on the ​shares.

Rhythm ​develops therapies for rare neuroendocrine disorders, while Alexion specializes ​in treatments for rare diseases and has ‌become the centerpiece of AstraZeneca's efforts to expand in high-growth specialty medicines.

AstraZeneca had previously expressed interest in Rhythm, which develops treatments for rare metabolic disorders and severe obesity, and renewed its pursuit in recent months, the Wall Street Journal reported.

In March, the US Food and Drug Administration expanded the use of Rhythm's therapy, Imcivree, for a rare form of obesity caused by brain damage, ‌making it the first treatment to be approved in ​the country for the condition.

The company is also developing treatments ​for additional rare neuroendocrine and metabolic diseases.

The ​obesity drug market has become one of the pharmaceutical industry's most coveted ‌sectors, driven by strong demand for treatments ​from Novo Nordisk and Eli ​Lilly and expectations that sales could exceed $100 billion annually over the next decade.

While Rhythm's therapies target rare genetic forms of obesity rather than the broader weight-loss market, an acquisition ​would give AstraZeneca an established ‌commercial presence in the fast-growing field while expanding its rare-disease portfolio.

(Reporting by Sabrina Valle ​and Milana Vinn in New York, Amy-Jo Crowley in London and Siddhi Mahatole in ​Bengaluru; Editing by Leroy Leo and Jamie Freed)
authors: By Sabrina Valle, Milana Vinn and Amy-Jo Crowley

articles.title: 'Imposto do pecado': o que é e como vai funcionar a tributação sobre produtos prejudiciais à saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Criado pela reforma tributária, o chamado Imposto Seletivo vai incidir sobre itens como bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros, além de produtos e atividades associados a danos ao meio ambiente. Nesta quarta-feira, o governo assinou e enviou ao Congresso uma MP sobre o tema.
articles.summary: Criado pela reforma tributária, o chamado Imposto Seletivo vai incidir sobre itens como bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros, além de produtos e atividades associados a danos ao meio ambiente. Nesta quarta-feira, o governo assinou e enviou ao Congresso uma MP sobre o tema.
articles.body:
Bebidas alcóolicas terão incidência do 'imposto do pecado'. — Foto: Rafael Leal/g1

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) assinou nesta quarta-feira (4) e enviou ao Congresso Nacional a medida provisória (MP) que define as regras de cobrança do Imposto Seletivo, também conhecido como o "imposto do pecado".

O tributo, que foi aprovado no âmbito da reforma tributária sobre o consumo, começa a ser cobrado em 2027 e tem o objetivo de encarecer produtos ou atividades que causam danos à saúde ou ao meio ambiente, como forma de reduzir a demanda.

A lista inclui bebidas alcoólicas , refrigerantes e cigarros . Também vai incidir sobre alguns veículos, conforme o nível de poluição , sobre a extração de bens minerais , e sobre loterias , apostas e jogos de fantasy sports.

Segundo o governo, a proposta enviada nesta quarta-feira prevê, para 2027, a manutenção da carga tributária atual sobre esses itens , por se tratar de período de transição. A partir de 2028, a ideia é que a taxação aumente.

A forma de cobrança varia de acordo com o produto ou a atividade.

No caso das bebidas alcoólicas , por exemplo, a tributação será maior quanto maior for o teor alcoólico da bebida.

Já para os veículos , a alíquota poderá variar conforme critérios relacionados ao nível de poluição.

O imposto não será cobrado sucessivamente em todas as etapas da cadeia. A legislação determina que ele incida apenas uma vez sobre cada bem ou serviço. Assim, o tributo não será acumulado a cada etapa de fabricação e comercialização até chegar ao consumidor.

Embora esteja previsto para 2027, o Imposto Seletivo não começará a ser cobrado imediatamente no início do ano.

O tributo está sujeito à chamada noventena, que estabelece um intervalo de 90 dias antes do início da cobrança. Segundo o governo, esse período deve se estender provavelmente até fevereiro de 2027.

Até lá, o Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI) continuará sendo cobrado sobre esses produtos, como forma de evitar uma perda de arrecadação durante a transição.

Para 2027, a equipe econômica estima arrecadar R$ 41,9 bilhões com esse tributo , segundo a proposta de Orçamento enviada ao Congresso.

Com a cobrança do Imposto Seletivo e da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), outro tributo criado pela reforma e que começará a ser cobrado no ano que vem, o governo busca manter a arrecadação estável em relação ao Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

O que dizem estudos sobre produtos afetados?

➡️ Álcool: estudo da Fiocruz citado pelo Ministério da Saúde estima que o consumo gerou R$ 18,8 bilhões em custos em 2019 , sendo R$ 1,1 bilhão em gastos federais com saúde e R$ 17,7 bilhões em perda de produtividade causada por mortes prematuras, afastamentos do trabalho e outros fatores.

➡️ Cigarros: doenças relacionadas ao tabagismo geram R$ 153,5 bilhões em custos por ano , segundo o Ministério da Saúde, considerando impactos diretos e indiretos. A arrecadação federal com a venda de cigarros, por sua vez, é de cerca de R$ 8 bilhões anuais.

➡️ Bebidas ultraprocessadas: o tratamento de doenças associadas ao consumo de produtos como refrigerantes, isotônicos e refrescos custa quase R$ 3 bilhões por ano ao SUS , segundo estudo usado pelo governo para embasar o Imposto Seletivo.

Produtores de bebidas alcoólicas, por outro lado, afirmam que o setor já é altamente tributado e que novos aumentos podem elevar preços, reduzir margens, provocar demissões e estimular o mercado ilegal. Segundo o setor, os impostos representam de 40% a mais de 80% do preço das bebidas.

articles.title: Nota Legal DF sorteia prêmios de até R$ 1 milhão nesta quinta (5) | G1
articles.standfirst: Sorteio terá transmissão ao vivo, a partir das 15h. Serão sorteados 12,6 mil bilhetes, somando um total de R$ 3,5 milhões em prêmios.
articles.summary: Quase 1,2 milhão de consumidores estão aptos a participar. Contemplados devem registrar os dados bancários no site do programa até 4 de fevereiro de 2027.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa Nota Legal — Foto: Reprodução/Nota Legal

O segundo sorteio de 2026 do Nota Legal no Distrito Federal será nesta quinta-feira (5). O prêmio principal é de R$ 1 milhão .

O sorteio terá transmissão ao vivo a partir das 15h nos canais da Secretaria de Economia do DF. Ao todo, serão sorteados 12,6 mil bilhetes, somando um total de R$ 3,5 milhões em prêmios ( veja detalhes mais abaixo ).

Nesta edição, quase 1,2 milhão de consumidores estão aptos a participar do sorteio. Concorrem:

consumidores que pediram a inclusão do CPF na nota fiscal, no período de novembro de 2025 a abril de 2026;

que estão adimplentes com a Secretaria de Economia, no período de 5 de agosto a 4 de setembro.

Os premiados devem acessar o site do Nota Legal e informar os dados bancários até 4 de fevereiro de 2027.

A secretária informa que o recebimento será por ordem de registro dos dados bancários no site do Nota Legal até o dia 4 de fevereiro de 2027.

Depois da data, não será mais permitido o envio das informações bancárias, e o dinheiro retorna ao Tesouro do DF.

Os valores sorteados serão depositados a partir da disponibilidade de caixa no início do semestre de 2027.

Além do recebimento em conta, o consumidor também pode pedir o resgate em conta bancária e abater no pagamento do IPTU ou do IPVA do próprio contribuinte (mesmo que sejam débitos antigos destes impostos).

articles.title: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows as Trump loses US midterm elections
articles.summary: Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.
articles.body: Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90, as markets continued to react to the political fallout of the US midterm elections and the possibility of an end to the war with Iran.Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 a barrel, while WTI crude declined 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.The latest movement follows Wednesday's sharp sell-off, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 a barrel, shedding $8.98 or 8.7%, while WTI settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3%. Both contracts recorded their lowest closing levels since August 31.The market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that US President Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.The election outcome has also complicated Washington's options in the conflict. With Democrats taking control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump could find it harder to pursue further military action. Two sources close to Gulf government circles told Reuters that the weakened political position gave him greater reason to pursue a negotiated settlement, making a full-scale assault on Iran less likely.However, the possibility of a deal does not necessarily rule out further escalation. Gulf analysts said an agreement that allows Iran to claim a clear victory while leaving Trump appearing defeated could encourage recklessness rather than restraint.Trump faces pressure as war weighs on RepublicansTrump told the Financial Times earlier this week that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. A day later, he acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections.Vice president JD Vance also questioned the decision to enter the war on Wednesday, distancing himself from it and blaming the conflict entirely for the Republicans' electoral setback.Tehran, however, has indicated that a change in political control in Washington would not alter its position towards the US. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that American hostility would continue regardless of which party was in power.There were also fresh developments in the region, with Yemen's Houthis claiming to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.Qatar steps up mediation as Iran deal remains distantDiplomatic efforts to prevent another escalation have gathered pace, with Qatar stepping up mediation following the US elections. But the prospect of an immediate breakthrough remains uncertain.Meanwhile, regional energy flows continue to be disrupted. The United Arab Emirates is also looking at ways to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, considering a third oil pipeline.Separately, US oil stockpiles recorded a decline last week. The Energy Information Administration said crude inventories dropped by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended October 30. This was sharply different from expectations in a Reuters poll, where analysts had forecast an increase of 877,000 barrels.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Stock Market Today Live Updates: BSE Sensex jumps 1,500 points, NSE Nifty50 trades above 24,400
articles.summary: The outlook for stock market remains closely linked to developments in global markets, particularly the sharp movement in crude oil prices following
articles.body: Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps over 1,400 points as FIIs fuel the rally The market rally extended beyond the benchmark indices, with mid-cap and small-cap stocks also joining the party. The Nifty Midcap 100 climbed 1.46%, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 1.49%. The Nifty 100 also advanced 1.78%. Among sectoral indices, Nifty Private Bank led the gains with a 2.55% rise, followed by Nifty Realty at 1.92%. Nifty IT advanced 1.72%, Nifty Auto gained 1.66%, Nifty Consumer Durables rose 1.52% and Nifty Media climbed 1.36%. Nifty FMCG also ended 1.08% higher. The renewed participation of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) added to the market's strength. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said, "Foreign institutional investors have returned as significant buyers, the revival in overseas fund flows marks an encouraging development for domestic equities, particularly as sustained institutional participation could lend greater depth to the ongoing market recovery".Stock market today: Why are NSE Nifty50 and BSE Sensex rising Indian equity markets staged a strong rally on Thursday, as falling crude oil prices and a revival in foreign investor buying boosted market sentiment. The positive momentum came against the backdrop of improving global sentiment after the November 2026 US midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party secured control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, dealing a significant setback to US President Donald Trump's administration. Adding to the cheer, Brent crude prices slipped below the $100-per-barrel mark to around $94 at the time of reporting. The decline offered some relief to India, which relies heavily on oil imports, while supporting domestic equities. Foreign fund inflows provided another boost, with overseas investors pumping around Rs 17,235 crore into Indian equities over just three trading sessions in November, signalling a return of institutional buying..Stock market today: Sensex soars over 1,500 points as Dalal Street extends rally Equity benchmarks continued their winning run on Thursday, with BSE Sensex surging 1,510.81 points, or 1.95%, to 78,812.21. NSE Nifty 50 also climbed 423.20 points, or 1.77%, to 24,344.10. According to Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, "The sharp advance reflects improving global risk sentiment, supported by lower crude prices and renewed institutional buying. However, the ability of the benchmarks to sustain these gains beyond the opening trades will be crucial in determining whether the positive momentum can translate into a broader upward move. Crude oil prices have retreated sharply; the decline offers some relief to an oil-import-dependent economy such as India". .Stock market today: Rupee adds to Dalal Street's momentum, opens at two-week high The rupee strengthened 0.3% from its previous close to open at a two-week high of 94.35 against the US dollar on Thursday, tracking a sharp slump in crude oil prices. The currency's gains added to the positive sentiment on Dalal Street, with benchmark indices extending their winning streak to six consecutive sessions..Stock market today: BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 soar in opening trade Dalal Street began Thursday on a strong note with both indices jumping sharply, Sensex gaining a whopping 1,400 points and Nifty50 rising over 1%. BSE Sensex opened 1,364.35 points, or 1.76%, higher at 78,665.75, while NSE Nifty50 climbed 374 points, or 1.56%, to 24,334.60..Stock market today: Top stocks to buy on November 5 Market expert shares his outlook for the trading session on November 5, along with his top stock picks and investment recommendations for the day. .Stock market today: Dalal Street set for positive start as GIFT Nifty signals gains Equity benchmarks might be headed for a positive opening on Thursday, tracking the sharp decline in international crude oil prices and gains across global markets. GIFT Nifty futures stood at 24,295.5, indicating a higher start for the Nifty 50, which had closed at 23,960.6 in the previous session. Brent crude futures declined another 1% to $93.5 per barrel after falling 8.7% in the previous session. The correction followed the US midterm election outcome, with investors assessing whether the Democrats' victory could accelerate efforts to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. Foreign fund flows remained another important domestic market factor. Provisional data showed that foreign investors purchased Indian shares worth Rs 72.84 billion ($769.65 million) on Wednesday. This marked their fourth consecutive session of buying, indicating a return of foreign participation following a substantial sell-off in Indian equities earlier in the year..Stock market today: Asian markets gain after US rally; Kospi slides 2.7% on chip stock concerns Asian equities advanced, tracking gains on Wall Street after the US midterm election results, with a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress coinciding with a sharp correction in crude oil prices. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.3%, supported by gains in benchmark indexes across Japan and Australia. The broader regional advance followed a strong session in the US. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, marking its biggest single-session gain in three months, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.9%. South Korea moved in the opposite direction, with the Kospi Index declining 2.7%. Investor concerns surrounding the future of data-centre development and losses in US semiconductor stocks weighed on the benchmark. US Treasuries extended their gains amid optimism that lower oil prices could help contain inflation. The dollar weakened for a second consecutive day, while US oil futures held on to their declines in early Thursday trade after Brent crude had fallen more than 8% in the previous session. Treasuries also gained across the yield curve as investors reduced bets on Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes over the coming year. The dollar recorded its steepest decline in two months..Stock market today: Crude crashes below $100 to hit multi-month lows after US midterm results International crude oil prices witnessed a sharp correction following the US midterm election results, with both Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures falling below the $100-per-barrel mark. Brent crude declined $9.27, or 8.9%, to $94.29 a barrel, touching its lowest level since September 4. US WTI futures dropped $7.44, or 7.8%, to $88.54. However, industry executives cautioned that the decline in prices may not necessarily translate into a sustained easing, as US President Donald Trump's weakened political position could complicate efforts to end the Iran war. Democrats' control of Congress could constrain funding for the conflict, while Trump may seek to demonstrate strength by intensifying military operations against Tehran. Executives said an escalation involving ground forces could prolong the conflict, disrupt energy supplies and raise costs for consumers. A decisive outcome, whether through military action or a negotiated deal, was considered preferable to a prolonged stalemate that continues to weigh heavily on oil importers..Stock market today: Rupee in focus after ending previous sessions with modest gains Rupee ended Wednesday's session with modest gains against the US dollar, supported by a weaker greenback and lower crude oil prices. The currency settled at 94.64 per dollar, compared with its previous close of 94.74, as investors assessed the implications of the US midterm election results. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of six major currencies, declined 0.4% to 101.3. The euro, sterling and Swiss franc were among the currencies registering gains against the greenback. Rupee had touched a two-week high during early trade but subsequently pared some of its gains as importer and interbank dollar bids gathered strength around the 94.50 mark..Stock market recap: Sensex rallies 4,000 points in five sessions, closes above 77,000; Nifty ends at 23,961 Stock market extended its winning streak for the fifth consecutive session on Wednesday, with the Sensex climbing nearly 384 points to close above the 77,000 mark. Buying in blue-chip financial, FMCG and automobile stocks, continued foreign fund inflows and easing crude oil prices supported the rally. The BSE Sensex gained 384 points to settle at 77,301, its highest closing level in more than two months. During the session, the index had surged as much as 478 points to touch 77,396. The five-session rally has added more than 4,000 points, or 5%, to the benchmark. The NSE Nifty also advanced 150 points to close at 23,961. Among Sensex constituents, Bharat Electronics, Titan, InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance, ITC and Adani Ports emerged as the biggest gainers. On the other hand, Tata Consultancy Services, HCL Tech, Infosys and Eternal were among the laggards. Foreign institutional investors purchased equities worth Rs 6,837 crore on Tuesday, according to exchange data. Brent crude, meanwhile, declined 0.7% to $102.8 per barrel. Market participants also pointed to improving global sentiment following the US midterm election outcome, which raised expectations of a more measured approach to trade and tariff policies and potentially stronger foreign fund flows into emerging markets. Mid- and small-cap stocks also extended their outperformance amid improving risk appetite.

articles.title: Democratic win may soften US immigration rhetoric; no immediate H-1B relief
articles.summary: Democratic Congress win may soften US immigration rhetoric but bring no immediate H-1B relief, as Trump can veto bills and act via executive rules.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A Democratic majority in Congress may shift the tone of the US immigration debate, but it is unlikely to bring immediate policy relief for Indian technology professionals or employers.However, experts believe a Democratic victory could help temper anti-immigrant sentiment and the political rhetoric targeting Indian technology professionals, creating a more favourable environment for skilled immigration and potentially laying the groundwork for policy changes in the longer term.Stephen Yale-Loehr, retired professor of immigration law practice at Cornell Law School, said a change in congressional control would not immediately translate into immigration reform.“President Trump is still president, and he controls the immigration agencies. Even if the Democrats pass positive immigration laws, President Trump can veto them. However, the Democrats can hold hearings and investigations to try to persuade the US public that immigration benefits, not hurts, the country. That way they will lay the groundwork for possible true immigration reform in 2029, assuming the Democrats control Congress then and there is a Democratic president then,” he said.David J Bier, director of Immigration Studies at Cato Institute, echoed this assessment, saying the election outcome would have almost no immediate impact on immigration policy. “It will have almost no immediate effect because Republicans still have enough votes to block most immigration bills in the Senate, and even if they didn’t, Trump would veto bills that block his agenda,” he said. Cyrus D Mehta, managing partner of New York-based law firm Cyrus D Mehta & Partners, said that even if Democrats take control of both houses of Congress, Trump would retain executive powers and could issue rules supporting the increase in H-1B fees to more than $100,000, along with other restrictions on the H-1B and green card programmes.“Trump will not be able to get legislation through Congress to endorse his executive actions if there are no Republican majorities. In any event, it would have been difficult for him to do so even now without 60 votes in the Senate. If the new Democratic majorities pass bills in Congress in 2026, Trump will have the power to veto them,” Mehta said.However, he said, officials in the Trump administration would face greater scrutiny and would need to justify their positions and policies before congressional oversight committees. If the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) denies H-1B petitions without justifiable grounds, such decisions could also come under investigation.“Also, since Texas and Georgia have become Democratic, they will no longer side with Trump in litigation against the $100,000 fee. This will leave the administration with less support in defending its policies in court,” he said.For Indian IT companies, which have traditionally relied on H-1B visas to deploy skilled professionals to the US, the debate comes amid a gradual shift towards local hiring and a reduced dependence on overseas work visas. Indian technology companies have significantly expanded their US-based workforce over the years, building a stronger domestic talent pool.According to IT industry body Nasscom, the number of H-1B visas issued to leading Indian and India-centric companies fell from 14,792 in 2015 to 10,162 in 2024. India’s largest IT services company, TCS, had around 11,000 H-1B employees within its 32,000-33,000-strong US workforce as of October last year.Microsoft said 80% of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications it filed in the last fiscal year were for extensions or changes in the status of existing employees. Applications for new hires accounted for just 1% of its US workforce and involved individuals already legally present in the country.Nasscom has maintained that H-1B is a high-skilled worker mobility programme and a non-immigrant visa that helps bridge critical skills gaps in the US. Indian technology companies contribute about $103 billion to the US economy and support more than 500,000 jobs across over 25 states, according to the industry body.Research has also challenged the argument that H-1B visa holders displace American workers. National Foundation for American Policy’s (NFAP) latest research cited a study by economist Madeline Zavodny, which found that H-1B visa holders do not adversely affect US workers. Instead, their presence is associated with lower unemployment rates and faster earnings growth among college graduates, including recent graduates.The research also found that a one-percentage-point increase in the share of workers with H-1B visas in an occupation was associated with an increase of 0.1 to 0.26 percentage points in the earnings growth rate for workers in that occupation.Other research cited by NFAP suggests that restricting H-1B visas could also have wider employment consequences. It estimated that if 178,000 H-1B applications had not been rejected in 2007 and 2008 because of the annual cap, US metropolitan areas could have created as many as 231,224 additional jobs for US-born technology workers. Many of these jobs could have gone to workers without college degrees.Based on H-1B petitions in computer-related occupations rejected by US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) in FY24 and FY25 because of the annual cap, NFAP estimated that a substantially higher annual limit could have supported the creation of up to 615,000 additional jobs for US-born technology workers.Immigration could also have fiscal benefits. Research by former Congressional Budget Office director Douglas Elmendorf and Dartmouth economics professor Heidi Williams found that exempting STEM master’s and PhD holders from employment-based green card limits could reduce the US federal budget deficit by $634 billion over 20 years.You use AI every day. articles.title: Diwali bonanza on Dalal Street: Investors add over Rs 6.9 lakh crore; top reasons behind Sensex, Nifty rally
articles.summary: Stock market today: Dalal Street brought an early Diwali bonanza for investors on Thursday, with Sensex soaring over 1,600 points and Nifty50 gaining 2%
articles.body: Stock market today: Dalal Street brought an early Diwali bonanza for investors on Thursday, with Sensex soaring over 1,600 points and Nifty50 gaining 2% in early trade. The rally added over Rs 6.9 lakh crore to investors' wealth, as easing crude oil prices, renewed foreign investor buying and improving global sentiment following the US midterm election results lifted market mood.The 30-share BSE Sensex surged 1,609.54 points, or 2.08%, to 78,910.94, while NSE Nifty50 advanced 417.45 points, or 1.74%, to settle at 24,378.05.Dalal Street extended its winning streak to six consecutive sessions on Thursday, building on Wednesday's gains when the Sensex climbed nearly 384 points to close at 77,301, its highest level in more than two months. The Nifty also advanced 150 points to settle at 23,961. The five-session rally through Wednesday had already lifted Sensex by over 4,000 points, or 5%.Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, told ANI, "The sharp advance reflects improving global risk sentiment, supported by lower crude prices and renewed institutional buying.”Here are the top reasons behind market rally:1. Crude oil prices slide below $95Falling crude oil prices remained one of the biggest factors supporting domestic equities on Thursday. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, slipped below $95 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell below $90.Brent crude futures declined 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 per barrel, while WTI crude fell 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.The latest decline followed a sharp sell-off on Wednesday, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 per barrel, shedding $8.98, or 8.7%, whileThe decline in oil prices offered relief to India, as the economy is dependent on oil imports, and supported sentiment in domestic equities.2. US midterm election results improve global sentimentThe outcome of the November 2026 US midterm elections also contributed to the positive mood across markets.The Democratic Party won control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, dealing a significant political setback to US President Donald Trump's administration.The election outcome raised expectations that Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end. With Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress, the US President could also find it harder to pursue further military action.Hopes of an end to the conflict supported the decline in crude oil prices and improved global risk sentiment.Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments Limited, told ANI, "The US midterm outcome improved global sentiment, raising expectations of a more measured approach to trade and tariff policies and potentially supporting FII flows into emerging markets,"3. Foreign investors return to Dalal StreetRenewed buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) provided another boost to domestic markets.Provisional data showed that foreign investors bought Indian shares worth Rs 72.84 billion ($769.65 million) on Wednesday, marking their fourth consecutive session of buying.Foreign investors also infused around Rs 17,235 crore into Indian equities in just three trading sessions in November, indicating a return of overseas institutional buying.The renewed inflows come against the backdrop of concerns over foreign investors' sustained exit from Indian markets. India's long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax has emerged as a pressing concern for investors, with the country's taxation regime being closely linked to the ongoing flight of foreign capital.India stands out internationally for taxing capital gains in the same country where the profits are generated. Reports suggest that most major stock markets globally either do not levy such a tax or tax the gains in the investor's home country.Commenting on the return of foreign investors, Ponmudi added, "Foreign institutional investors have returned as significant buyers, the revival in overseas fund flows marks an encouraging development for domestic equities, particularly as sustained institutional participation could lend greater depth to the ongoing market recovery."4. Rupee touches two-week highRupee also extended its gains against the US dollar, opening at a two-week high of 94.35 per dollar on Thursday, up 0.3% from its previous close.The currency rose 14 paise to 94.32 against the US dollar in early trade, after closing at 95.64 on Wednesday, marginally stronger than its previous close of 95.75.This marked the fifth consecutive session of gains for the currency.Meanwhile, the dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 101.18, down 0.53%.5. Broader markets and banking stocks join the rallyThursday's rally was broad-based, with buying seen across market segments, sectors and heavyweight stocks. Fourteen of the 16 major sectors ended in positive territory, while the broader mid-cap and small-cap indices also gained over 1% each.The Nifty Midcap 100 advanced 1.46%, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 rose 1.49%. The Nifty 100 also climbed 1.78%, reflecting the wider market rally.Among sectoral indices, Nifty Private Bank led the gains, rising 2.55%, followed by Nifty Realty at 1.92%. Nifty IT advanced 1.72%, Nifty Auto gained 1.66%, Nifty Consumer Durables rose 1.52% and Nifty Media climbed 1.36%. Nifty FMCG also ended 1.08% higher.On the Sensex, Bajaj Finance jumped 5.33%. Maruti Suzuki followed with a 4.94% rise, while InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) gained 4.88%. Asian Paints advanced 4.39%, M&M rose 3.89% and Infosys climbed 3.67%.Other notable gainers included Tech Mahindra (3.35%), HCL Technologies (3.13%), UltraTech Cement (2.88%), TCS (2.87%), ICICI Bank (2.81%) and Bajaj Finserv (2.63%).The latest gains extend the momentum seen over the previous week. Earlier on Wednesday, Sensex climbed 383.55 points, or 0.50%, to close at 77,301.40, its highest closing level in more than two months. NSE Nifty50 advanced 149.75 points, or 0.63%, to settle at 23,960.60. Among Sensex constituents, Bharat Electronics, Titan, InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance, ITC and Adani Ports were the biggest gainers, while TCS, HCL Tech, Infosys and Eternal featured among the laggards.However, Ponmudi cautioned that sustaining the gains beyond the initial trading hours would be key to determining whether the rally could develop into a broader market recovery. He also noted that the sharp correction in crude oil prices offered some much-needed relief to India as an oil-import-dependent economy.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. articles.title: Gold, silver price prediction: Will gold hit Rs 1.5 lakh in Dhanteras week? Check outlook on November 5, 2026
articles.summary: Gold and silver price prediction today: Gold and silver prices have recovered from recent lows but may face some upside resistance, says Abhilash
articles.body: Gold and silver price prediction today: Gold and silver prices have recovered from recent lows but may face some upside resistance, says Abhilash Koikkara, Head - Forex & Commodities, Nuvama Professional Clients Group. Here is his outlook:MCX Gold Price OutlookMCX Gold has rebounded from its recent lows following the market's reaction to the US Midterm Election results. Prices have managed to sustain above the long-term support zone formed by previous swing lows, which has been sustained since January 2026. The daily chart indicates a revival of buying interest post the event, suggesting that bullish momentum could strengthen further over the coming trading sessions.Gold is likely to face an immediate resistance around 147,500, coinciding with its 30-week exponential moving average. A sustained weekly close above 146,000 would reinforce the bullish outlook and potentially establish a fresh positive bias for the week ahead. On the downside, key support levels are placed at 140,000 and 138,000. However, a weekly close below 138,000 would invalidate the anticipated bullish setup and weaken the positive outlook.Following the recent reversal, gold prices started the week on a positive note, recovering from the previous week's lows and maintaining an upward bias. The bullish price action is further supported by favourable technical and momentum indicators, which reinforce the improved market outlook. Accordingly, a buy-on-dips strategy appears favourable heading into the festive week, with strict stop-loss placed below the previous week's low of 138,000.MCX Gold Trading StrategyCMP: Rs 143,200Target: Rs 150,000Stop Loss: Rs 138,000MCX Silver Price OutlookSimilar to gold, silver has recovered from its recent lows, supported by renewed buying interest, and is likely to maintain a positive bias during the coming week. The previous week's high will act as the immediate resistance and a decisive move above this level could make the way for a fresh intermediate bullish trend. Following the positive market reaction to the US Midterm Election results, prices are expected to build on the ongoing recovery and sustain their upward momentum in the sessions ahead.The recent recovery is expected to find support around the weekly low of 174,000, and a decisive break below this level could reinforce the existing bearish trend. As long as prices sustain above this support, the recovery may extend towards the previous breakdown zone of 210,000, with an immediate resistance placed around 198,000.Technical and momentum indicators on the daily charts suggest that the prevailing bearish momentum may be gradually losing strength, with both showing signs of recovery from lower levels.A cautious buy-on-dips approach may be considered, keeping the previous week's lows as the stoploss levels. However, the recent recovery could also be a short-term, news-driven reaction within the broader bearish trend. Hence, any fresh buying positions should be initiated with a strict stop-loss to manage downside risk.MCX Silver Trading StrategyCMP: Rs 187,700Target: Rs 210,000Stop Loss: Rs 174,000(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own.
